title: Flatten policy pipeline and implement non-blocking fallback orchestrator
creator: Anika Shah
description: We have accumulated complexity in the smart routing layer where policy evaluation, route selection, and fallback orchestration are tightly coupled and frequently lock on shared state. This ticket scopes a refactor to: (1) flatten the policy evaluation pipeline into a lightweight, pluggable evaluator chain that returns immutable decision blobs; (2) introduce a non-blocking fallback orchestrator that composes decisions and triggers asynchronous fallbacks without holding hot locks; (3) remove one global routing cache in favor of per-shard ephemeral caches with clear eviction semantics. The end goal is to reduce p95 request latency spikes under contention, simplify reasoning about policy changes, and make future regional isolation simpler to implement.
problem_statement: Current policy path acquires multiple locks at evaluation time, performing network calls and capacity checks inline. Under high concurrency this yields tail latency amplification and occasional route flapping when fallbacks are applied synchronously. The code is brittle to dependency upgrades (policy-compiler v2.x) and hard to test because of intertwined side effects.
goals: Eliminate nested locks on routing hotpath
Return immutable decision objects from policy evaluators
Implement non-blocking fallback orchestration that schedules fallbacks asynchronously
Reduce p95 latency by >=10% on our busiest routes
Make routing behavior deterministic and unit-testable
Reduce lines of hotpath code and remove direct usage of the global routing cache
constraints: Must preserve existing SLOs for latency and error-rate during rollout
Rollback must be possible via feature flag within 10 minutes
Behavioral changes to policy semantics require policy-tests to pass
No customer-visible config changes for Dedicated/Private customers in this change window
design_decisions: Introduce Decision struct (immutable) with fields: route, candidate_variants, score_vector, metadata (opaque)
Policy evaluators will be composed via a small EvalChain interface; evaluators must be pure functions (no side-effects)
Fallback orchestrator runs on a separate executor pool and uses a compare-and-swap update to install fallback routes into request context, avoiding global locks
Replace global routing cache with per-shard LRU caches keyed by request fingerprint; caches are advisory only (router consults cloud control plane for authoritative state)
Upgrade policy-compiler dependency to v2.1.0 and run compatibility shim during canary
Add telemetry hooks: decision_id (UUID), eval_duration_ms, fallback_latency_ms, and decision_source tag
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for EvalChain and Decision serializer/deserializer (coverage >= 90% for new code)
End-to-end integration test that reproduces previous locking scenario and validates reduced lock contention
Canary shows p95 drop >= 10% and no increase in error-rate after 48 hours (see benchmark dashboard)
Feature flag rollback successfully reverts behavior without restart
Conformance tests for Dedicated and Private deployments pass (routing behavior unchanged for pinned configs)
benchmark_summary: Baseline: busiest-route p95 = 183ms under synthetic load (1k rps, 200 concurrent connections)
After refactor (local perf runs): busiest-route p95 = 158ms (-13.7%)
Median unchanged (~35ms), p99 unchanged in synthetic single-shard runs (investigate further in multi-shard tests)
Lock contention sampling shows 45% less time spent in global routing mutex during stress test
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Introduce Decision type and EvalChain interface; add unit tests (branch: feature/ENG-86104/decision-eval)
Phase 2: Implement non-blocking fallback orchestrator behind feature flag and run local integration tests (executor pool size default = 32)
Phase 3: Replace global routing cache reads with per-shard cache adapters; run synthetic traffic job against staging
Phase 4: Upgrade policy-compiler to v2.1.0 and enable compatibility shim; deploy to canary region
Phase 5: 48-hour canary monitoring, collect SLOs and error budgets, then scoped gradual rollout to remaining regions
Phase 6: Remove backward-compat shim and old global cache code after successful rollout
migration_steps: Deploy Decision/EvalChain code with feature flag off
Deploy non-blocking orchestrator with feature flag off and run integration smoke tests
Enable caches in read-only advisory mode and run canary for 24 hours
Flip feature flag for one low-traffic region and monitor for 24 hours
If stable, incrementally enable for medium-traffic regions, then high-traffic; target full rollout in 2 weeks
After successful rollout, deprecate feature flag and remove old code path in next minor release
monitoring_and_rollout: Alerts: p95 increase > 5% for 30m, error_rate > baseline + 0.5% for 10m
Automated rollback: if canary region triggers either alert, rollback flag within 10 minutes
Tracing: add decision_id tag to existing traces to correlate policy-time with downstream latency
Cost: track any increase in CPU for orchestrator executor pool weekly
test_plan: Unit tests: pure evaluator behavior, Decision JSON serialization, cache eviction semantics
Integration tests: race-condition reproduction test that previously caused a deadlock
Load tests: 1k/5k/10k rps against multi-shard scenario (compare to baseline)
Conformance: Dedicated/Private deployment test suite (certify no behavioral regression)
